description: Adds RDKit physchem descriptors, quantile-transformed to normal (QuantileTransformer, n_quantiles=200) and fed to an SVR, then averages that SVR with the existing random forest on Morgan fingerprints; the RF stays on raw fingerprints.
Appends the 167 RDKit MACCS structural keys to the Morgan fingerprint matrix used by the random forest, leaving the descriptor-based SVR unchanged.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The diff only adds 167 MACCS structural keys after the Morgan bits, built from each molecule's own SMILES. It reads no files and uses no labels; train and test molecules are featurized the same way.
No bug found. GenMACCSKeys returns 167 bits, ConvertToNumpyArray fills the 167-length float32 array correctly, and every row has a fixed width of N_BITS+167. The extra work adds little runtime.

Recomputed z: the candidate mean is (0.6187+0.6241)/2 = 0.6214, and the incumbent is 0.6304 from 1 run, so the gain is 0.0090. The standard error is 0.0042*sqrt(1/2+1/1) = 0.00514, giving z = 1.75. That matches the harness value of 1.756; the small gap is most likely rounding of the adjusted values.

The evidence is borderline. z is about 1.75 and the incumbent has only one run, so part of the gain could come from a lucky incumbent draw. Both candidate runs beat the incumbent, and the change is simple and well-motivated, so accepting is reasonable.

description: Appends the 167 RDKit MACCS structural keys to the Morgan fingerprint matrix used by the random forest, leaving the descriptor-based SVR unchanged.

Adds a LightGBM L1 regressor on the Morgan+MACCS features, with 10% inner validation early stopping (100 rounds, max 3000 trees) and a final refit at 1.1x the best iteration, and averages it equally with the RF and SVR predictions.
Aborted: post-hoc linear recalibration via a 5-fold inner OOF on the full RF+SVR+LGB ensemble would multiply each fit's cost roughly 6x and likely breach the 10-minute job limit.
Enlarges the random forest to 1000 trees with min_samples_leaf=2 and max_features=0.2, keeping the Morgan+MACCS features, to reduce variance and regularize the leaves.

Replaces the random forest in the first ensemble member with a LightGBM L1-objective regressor (800 trees, lr 0.03, colsample 0.5, subsample 0.8) on the same Morgan+MACCS features, keeping the SVR and the existing LightGBM member unchanged.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The diff only swaps the RandomForestRegressor for an LGBMRegressor with an L1 objective, which matches the MAE loss. There is no file or network access, no hard-coded answers and no use of test labels. The model is fitted on train data only, and the seed goes to random_state.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. Both runs finished without integrity flags, so lgb must already be imported in the file. Cosmetic leftovers: the prediction is still named p_rf, and N_TREES, MAX_FEATURES and MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF may now be unused. Those constants should be removed or reused to keep the script simple.

Recomputed z: the candidate mean is 0.60225 (0.6007 and 0.6038), the incumbent is 0.6098 from 1 run, so the difference is 0.00755. The standard error is 0.0042 × sqrt(1/2 + 1/1) ≈ 0.00514, which gives z ≈ 1.47. The harness reports 1.461; the small gap is likely rounding of the adjusted values. The two agree.

The improvement (about 0.0075 MAE) points the right way but is not significant at the usual threshold, and the incumbent has only one run. The provisional reject fits the numbers. One more replicate of the candidate or the incumbent could settle it.

description: Replaces the random forest in the first ensemble member with a LightGBM L1-objective regressor (800 trees, lr 0.03, colsample 0.5, subsample 0.8) on the same Morgan+MACCS features, keeping the SVR and the existing LightGBM member unchanged.

Replaces the fixed equal-weight average of RF, SVR and LightGBM with a stacker: 5-fold inner OOF predictions from the three base models are combined by non-negative least squares (scipy nnls), and the base models are refit on all training data to blend test predictions with those weights.

Removes the nested inner 5-fold stacking loop, which ran about 90 base-model fits per job and caused the 600 s timeout, and averages the three base models with equal weights; the SEARCH text now matches the original file, and the LightGBM learning rate is doubled to cut its tree count.
Adds RDKit atom-pair and topological-torsion count fingerprints (1024 bits each) and switches the Morgan block to counts, concatenating all three with the MACCS keys in featurize.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The diff only changes featurize(). It switches Morgan from bits to counts and adds atom-pair and topological-torsion count fingerprints (1024 each) next to the MACCS keys. It reads no files and doesn't use test labels; featurization works one molecule at a time, so no test information leaks into training.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. All generators come from rdFingerprintGenerator, and GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy is a valid method. The feature matrix is about 3360 x 4263 float32, roughly 57 MB, which is well within the memory limit.
Recomputed z: (0.6098 - 0.6007) / (0.0042 * sqrt(1/2 + 1/1)) = 0.0091 / 0.00514 = 1.77. This matches the harness value of 1.767; the small gap comes from rounding.

Caveat: both candidate runs gave exactly 0.6007. If the replicate repeated the same seeds and folds, it was a deterministic re-run and adds no information about noise. In that case the effective n is 1 and z = 0.0091 / (0.0042 * sqrt(2)) = 1.53, which is still a likely improvement but a weaker one. The incumbent also has only one run.
Cost: the job now uses more features, so it will take longer, but it should stay well under the 10-minute limit. The code is still simple.

description: Adds RDKit atom-pair and topological-torsion count fingerprints (1024 bits each) and switches the Morgan block to counts, concatenating all three with the MACCS keys in featurize.

Appends counts of 10 ionizable-group SMARTS patterns (carboxylic acid, tetrazole, phenol, primary/secondary/tertiary aliphatic amine, amidine/guanidine, pyridine-type N, sulfonic acid, quaternary N) to the per-molecule feature vector used by the RF and LightGBM members.
Raises the Morgan fingerprint radius from 2 to 3 and its width from 2048 to 4096 bits, leaving the count featurizer and RandomForest unchanged.

Adds a CatBoost regressor (MAE loss, 1000 iterations, depth 6) on Morgan count fingerprints concatenated with the RDKit descriptors as a fourth member, averaged equally with the RF, SVR and LightGBM predictions.

issues: No integrity problem found. The diff only adds standard LightGBM regularization settings: subsample=0.7 with subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.4, min_child_samples=20 and reg_lambda=1.0. It adds no file or network access, no pasted answers and no use of test labels.

No bug found. Early stopping still uses an internal split of the training fold only (train_test_split on train_y). min_child_samples=20 is already LightGBM's default, so that setting is redundant but harmless.

My z check: the gain is 0.5679 - 0.5661 = 0.0018. One run per arm with noise sd 0.0042 gives a standard error of 0.0042*sqrt(2) ≈ 0.00594, so z ≈ 0.30. That matches the reported 0.310 within the rounding of the shown losses.

The gain is well inside the noise of a single run, so the provisional reject agrees with the numbers. One replicate could confirm it if the program wants these regularization settings, but the expected benefit is small.

description: Adds row bagging (subsample 0.7, subsample_freq 1), feature fraction 0.4, min_child_samples 20 and reg_lambda 1.0 to the LightGBM L1 member's parameters.
Proposed: average only RF, LightGBM L1 and a Tanimoto-kernel SVR, which would drop the current four-member average (RF, descriptor SVR, LightGBM, CatBoost).
Switches the random forest to sqrt feature sampling with bootstrap rows (max_samples=0.7) and 500 trees, to decorrelate trees on the redundant fingerprint features.

Switches the Morgan count fingerprint (radius 2, 2048 bits) to pharmacophoric feature atom invariants (donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen classes) so the ECFP-style fragments generalize better across unseen scaffolds.
